summary: Karl Richard Lepsius worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig (~1828–1830), Göttingen (~1830–1832), and Berlin (~1832–1833), and held posts at Berlin (~1846–1884) and as Chief Librarian at the Prussian State Library (~1873–1884).

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied under Hegel in Berlin (~1824–1826) and at Halle and Heidelberg. He held posts at Halle, including a chair of philosophy (~1830–1833), and served as professor and Rektor at Königsberg from 1833.

Linguist Karl Verner studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, the University of Copenhagen (~1864–1873), and under August Leskien (~1875–1876). He worked as a librarian in Halle (~1876–1883) and became Dozent für Slawistik at Copenhagen in 1882.
Karl von Hegel worked in history and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1841–1856) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1856–1893).

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Augsburg and the University of Munich, and held posts at Munich (1978–1988), the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy (1989–1991), and FHWS (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Bonn (~1976–1985) and completed his habilitation at Hamburg (~1993–1999). He was a Privatdozent at Hamburg in 1999 and worked at the Göttingen Academy (~2000–2018).
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as the main disciple under Anagarika Govinda, whom he succeeded in 1982.

Karlfried Graf Dürckheim worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kiel University (~1919–1923), he held posts at Leipzig (~1925–1930), Pädagogische Akademie Breslau (~1930–1932), Breslau (~1931–1932), and the Bauhaus.
Karma Drubgyü Ngedön Nyingpo studied under Pema Wangchok Gyelpo and Khakyab Dorje.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

A scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, Karma Lekshe Tsomo studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and at Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2023).
Karma Lodrö Chökyi Sengge worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche in 1973 and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Karma Phuntsho works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Oxford under Michael Aris, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Richard Gombrich, and held posts at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute (1994), CNRS (~2003–2005), and the University of Cambridge (~2003).
Karma Shedrub Chokyi Sengge studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and taught Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Karma Sonam Palmo specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed her PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot of the Young Lamas Home School (~1962) and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, Magdalen College, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (1999–2008).

Karsé Kongtrul studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, whom he also taught, alongside students Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and Professor of Sanskrit at Mahamakut Buddhist University.

Karunesh Shukla is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation and served as Professor and Head of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1991).
